current_route.title: QWOT-Reinitialized 29-Layer HfO2/MgF2 UV Bandpass with ±2.0 nm Perturbation Bounds
current_route.scientific_hypothesis: A 29-layer alternating HfO2/MgF2 stack initialized at quarter-wave optical thicknesses for 267 nm center wavelength, with thickness optimization bounded to ±2.0 nm per layer, will produce higher target scores than the previous highly-scaled parameter inheritance approach, because the QWOT initialization places the design in a physically meaningful region of the solution space where UV transmission and visible/NIR rejection are simultaneously achievable through first-order interference.
current_route.design_principle: Quarter-wave stacks create high reflectance at the design wavelength through constructive interference of reflections from each interface. For a bandpass filter, the stack is designed so that the UV band (255-280 nm) experiences transmission while longer wavelengths experience reflection. HfO2 (high index, ~2.0-2.1 in UV) and MgF2 (low index, ~1.38-1.40 in UV) provide sufficient index contrast for effective interference. Starting from QWOT thicknesses and limiting perturbations to ±2.0 nm keeps the optimizer near a physically sensible solution rather than allowing it to drift into numerically converged but physically unrealistic thickness regimes.
